reasoning: Data from the Lunar Laser Ranging experiment (which measures the round-trip travel time of laser light bounced off retroreflectors left on the Moon by Apollo astronauts) confirms that the Moon is currently receding from Earth at a rate of approximately 3.78 to 3.8 centimeters (about 1.5 inches) per year. This gradual retreat is caused by tidal friction: the gravitational pull of the Moon creates tidal bulges on Earth, and because Earth rotates faster than the Moon orbits, these bulges "pull" the Moon forward in its orbit, transferring angular momentum and pushing it into a higher, wider orbit.
